text:
incident-bot: PAGING: KV-cache eviction rate spiked to 18% in us-west-1-infer-2, continuous-batching latency >= 95th pct threshold. Paging oncall alex_w. Alerts: https://monitoring/redwood/alerts/3321 :rotating_light:

alex_w (oncall): ack — joining. pulling dashboards (kv entries, batch sizes, scheduler queues). will call if we need conference.

maya_s (sre): looking at scheduler logs now — seeing long tails on batch latency and very large batch sizes for some shards (batch_size > 300 occasionally). short requests are queuing for >500ms.

devon_p (runtime): KV cache cardinality exploded for many clients — unique prefix keys grew 12x in last 30m. suspect interaction between recent continuous-batching micro-optimizations and prefix caching.

alex_w (oncall): immediate mitigation plan: 1) temporarily disable continuous batching on the affected pool; 2) start rolling restart to flush kv cache if disabling doesn't drop memory; 3) notify customers. executing step 1 now.

alex_w (oncall): executing config change: 
```bash
curl -X POST 'https://console.redwood/api/v1/pools/us-west-1-infer-2/config' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer ${REDACTED}' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"continuous_batching": {"enabled": false}}'
```

deploy-bot: config change applied to pool us-west-1-infer-2 (change-id: cfg-2026-03-15-021). Rolling update started to pick up new config on workers.

maya_s (sre): after disabling continuous batching: batch sizes collapsed to expected ranges, tail latency dropped ~210ms at p99, but overall throughput dropped ~8% as expected. KV cache entries still high (GC not yet run).

devon_p (runtime): starting rolling restart of workers to flush in-memory KV state. command: `rb-admin restart --pool=us-west-1-infer-2 --rolling --grace=60s` (kicking off now).

deploy-bot: restart job started (job-id: restart-4491). Estimated completion ~12m.

paul_r (support): we have 3 customer tickets flagged in the last 30m referencing timeouts and 5xx errors (customers: Acme, NimbusApp, Gridly). Would like a short note to send.

alex_w (oncall): agreed — drafting interim message: "We detected a regression affecting our continuous-batching path that caused cache growth and higher tail latencies. Mitigations (disabling continuous batching + rolling restart) are in progress; you may experience transient rate-limited errors — we will follow up with a timeline once restarts finish." Will paste into #customer-comms once finalized.

ops-rotation: incoming handoff (30m). please include checklist for postmortem: root-cause, config diff, backlog of affected requests, customer-impact table, and runbook updates to avoid regression.

maya_s (sre): digging into root cause: a recent change to batching_timeout_ms (commit 18f3a9) reduced the aggressiveness of per-request-size gating. That combined with a change in kv_cache.policy to keep more prefix entries created a positive feedback loop: long streaming requests caused larger batches which created many unique cache prefixes, which prevented effective KV reuse -> cache blowup.

devon_p (runtime): reproduced locally with mixed workload (short QPS + rare long streams). scheduler fairness favored large-batch grouping because batching window increased slightly; short requests got starved. Proposed hotfix: revert batching_timeout_ms to previous value AND add per-request-length bucketed queues (short vs long) with token-based weighted fairness. Example config: 
```json
{"scheduler": {"fairness_mode": "weighted", "short_request_weight": 2, "long_request_weight": 1},
 "kv_cache": {"max_entries_per_client": 1000}}
```

alex_w (oncall): plan: 1) canary revert of batching_timeout_ms to commit before 18f3a9 on 2 nodes; 2) if stable for 10m, roll to pool; 3) follow-up with a proper scheduler fairness change in next patch. triggering canary revert now.

deploy-bot: revert applied to canary nodes (node-7,node-8). monitoring for 10m.

maya_s (sre): canary metrics: p99 latency back to baseline, short-request queue lengths cleared, KV cache growth rate stopped and now decaying. looks good after ~6m.

devon_p (runtime): scheduling global revert and scheduling a small config improvement PR for bucketed queues and per-client cache limits. I'll open PR with tests for mixed long/short workloads.

paul_r (support): drafted customer update and included mitigation details + ETA. Asked to add affected customers list — I will follow up after I have final numbers.

alex_w (oncall): restart job completed; overall pool healthy. final immediate status: continuous batching disabled (temp), batching_timeout_ms reverted in canary then pool-wide revert in progress, rolling restart completed. Impact: moderate (elevated errors for ~40 minutes), currently stabilized.

ops-rotation: handing off to maya_s for next 2 hours to watch the metrics and start the postmortem. maya, please track: exact commits involved, config diffs, customer impact table, and a mitigation timeline.

maya_s (sre): taking handoff. initial notes for postmortem: cause = batching_timeout_ms regression (commit 18f3a9) + kv_cache.policy change; effects = cache cardinality spike, batch scheduler starvation of short requests, tail latency spike, transient customer errors; mitigations = revert + rolling restart + temp disable of continuous batching; follow-ups = add fairness queues, per-client cache caps, add a Canary that runs a mixed-workload simulation on config changes, update runbook to include this pattern.

devon_p (runtime): I'll attach reproducer and automated test to the PR and add a load test that simulates 95% short + 5% long streams to guard against future regressions.

alex_w (oncall): thanks all. I'll post an incident summary to #postmortems when we have the final customer-impact counts and timing. For anyone coming in later: the active mitigations are complete and metrics are green, but please do not re-enable continuous batching globally until the scheduler fairness changes land and pass canary. :thumbsup:

paul_r (support): will update the tickets and notify affected customers. keeping thread for follow-up.

incident-bot: Incident status changed to "mitigated" (incident-3321). Next update expected in 6h with postmortem link.

maya_s (sre): note for postmortem: add suggested automated alert for sudden increase in KV unique prefixes and an indicator that long-batch dominance is occurring (e.g., % of batches > N over sliding window).

alex_w (oncall): handing off final to maya_s. dropping off.

maya_s (sre): will run the postmortem + send calendar invite for incident review. closing thread for paging; keep it open for postmortem comments.
